_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401884736.overall: Bayern are top with 21 points from nine games and host 15th-placed Cologne, who have not won in four league games and scored only two goals in that run. Vincent Kompany returns to the touchline for the first time since collapsing on 23 October; at Thursday's press conference he said Musiala is available and will probably be involved, while Luis Díaz is not ready yet (he hopes within seven days) and Davies, Neuer, Gnabry and Saibari stay out, all already counted by the numbers. Cologne's René Wagner is without Dallinga, Hübers, Skhiri, van den Berg and Rondic (all counted) and is expected to set up with a back five, with Ache fit but likely on the bench. Robin Braun referees, and his above-average card record is already in the numbers. Match-day check: no new injuries or surprises, so the view is unchanged.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and already take about 12% off Bayern's attack for Díaz and Musiala as if both are fully out. Kompany confirmed on Thursday that Díaz is still a week away but Musiala is available and will probably play some part, which the numbers don't see, so I nudge up just 1%, to about 3.74. Cologne without Dallinga and Skhiri is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, with Bayern's recent run of corners (37 in six) already added. Cologne are expected to line up with a back five and defend deep, then break quickly, which is the one-sided pattern the numbers already expect, so I stay at 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already add about 9% for referee Robin Braun (4.4 cards a game against a 3.9 average) plus Cologne's high recent card count (17 in six). Wagner wants his players to 'go where it hurts', but that fits the same pattern the numbers count, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.0 shots and already add 7.5% for Bayern's hot shooting run (127 shots in six). Bayern's attack around Kane, Olise, Karl and Brown is near full strength apart from Díaz, who is counted, so I stay at 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.4 shots on target, already lifted 11% for Bayern's recent accuracy. Musiala off the bench adds a little, but that is in the small goals nudge, and Cologne's weak attack without Dallinga is counted, so I stay at 12.4.

401884732.overall: Union are 16th with one win in their last six and only 48 shots in that run, and Steffen Baumgart's side face Leipzig, 4th with four wins in five, who lost to Real Madrid and Manchester City in the Champions League recently and have more European games to come. Union's doubts are still long: Comunio (19 Nov) lists Uduokhai, Haberer (ill), captain Trimmel, Burcu and Skov as doubtful, with Nsoki and Markgraf out; Sports Mole also says Haberer could miss it. One change since this morning: Juranovic, whom the numbers count as out (about -8% on Union's goals), is in the predicted lineups of Sports Mole and the Bundesliga's own site. Leipzig miss Guiu and Ouedraogo (counted), while Finkgraefe is close to a return and Konate and Kaltefleiter are doubtful. Christian Dingert referees; his near-average record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and take about 8% off Union for Juranovic, who now appears in two predicted lineups, so that cut may be too big. Against that, Haberer is still ill and doubtful and Trimmel, Burcu and Uduokhai are uncertain, none of which the numbers count, so I go 3% lower, to about 2.8 (was -5).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already cut for both sides' low recent corner counts (Union 18, Leipzig 22 in six). Union's absences change who plays rather than how they attack, and Leipzig usually win corners through Nusa and Raum down the flanks, which the numbers see, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards and already add Union's rough recent run (18 cards in six) while trimming a little for referee Christian Dingert, who shows about 3.8 a game. A reshuffled Union side under pressure at home may foul a bit more, but that is the same pattern the numbers already add for, so I stay at 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.1 shots and already cut Union's shots 13% for their recent drought. Haberer's illness and the doubts over Burcu and Trimmel thin Union's attack further, while Juranovic's likely return helps a little, so I go 3% lower, to about 24.3 (was -4).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, with Leipzig's recent accuracy (+8%) already counted. Same reasons as shots: Union may be without Haberer and others who are doubtful, partly offset by Juranovic, so I go 3% lower, to about 9.0 (was -4).

401884735.overall: Leverkusen are 5th and host Paderborn, 13th with one loss in five. The news on Leverkusen keeps improving: coach Carles Martinez said on Friday that Maza is available after his ankle problem with Algeria and that everyone in the squad can start, and Bulinews reports Terrier as the only confirmed absence, with Diaby, Kofane, Doue and Eichhorn all possible (Comunio still lists Eichhorn out). The numbers still count Diaby, Tella, Doue and Eichhorn as missing, and the Bundesliga's predicted lineup has both Maza and Diaby starting. Paderborn are without Gayret, with Baack and Scheller doubtful and Pieringer possibly back. Tobias Reichel referees and his near-average record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and take about 3% off Leverkusen for Diaby, who is now in the predicted lineup, while Maza has also been cleared and Kofane and Tella are back, none of which the numbers see. Terrier is still out, so I go 4% higher, to about 2.7 (was +3; Maza's fitness is the change).

corners.text: The numbers say 11.4 corners, with Leverkusen expected to have most of the ball against a Paderborn back three that sits deep. Returning forwards change who finishes moves more than how often Leverkusen attack down the flanks, so I stay at 11.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, with referee Reichel (4.0 a game) adding about 3%. Paderborn's low recent card count is already in the numbers and nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.8 shots, already lifted slightly for both sides' recent volume. Leverkusen kept shooting a lot (102 in six) even with forwards missing, so the returns of Maza and Diaby mostly help quality, not volume, and I stay at 31.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. With Maza cleared and Diaby, Kofane and Tella back, Leverkusen's finishing options are better than the numbers assume, so I go 3% higher, to about 10.6 (was +2).

401884731.overall: Bottom side Gladbach (one win under Alexander Blessin) host Dortmund, 2nd, unbeaten and level on 21 points with Bayern. Gladbach are without the banned Itakura and the injured Kleindienst, Leopold, Leszczynski, Ullrich and, per Bulinews, Hashioka; goalkeeper Nicolas is fit again. Only Bolin and Ullrich move the numbers' goals, and Kleindienst has been out for weeks, so his absence is largely in Gladbach's form. For Dortmund, Can, Konstantelias, Lerma and Chukwuemeka are out, while Guirassy (thigh strain) and Anton (muscle problems) are doubtful: Niko Kovac said it is 'not ruled out' they play and that whoever is fit will play, and the Bundesliga's predicted lineup includes both, so this morning's rotation worry looks smaller. Robert Hartmann referees and his record is close to average.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, already taking Bolin and Ullrich off Gladbach. I lean 2% lower, to about 2.7: Guirassy is still only doubtful after his thigh strain and Gladbach's attack lacks Kleindienst. I cut this morning's -3 because Kovac says whoever is fit will play, so heavy rotation before the Champions League looks unlikely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already nudged up for Dortmund's recent count (37 in six). Gladbach plan to defend in a back three and break, which the numbers already expect, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards and already add a big 22% for Gladbach's recent card spike (21 in six), including Itakura's yellow-red that bans him here. Blessin wants an aggressive game in a full stadium, but that is the same pattern the numbers already add for, and referee Hartmann (4.0 a game) is close to average, so I stay at 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting. With Kovac planning to play his fit first-choice players and Guirassy possibly back, the Dortmund rotation I allowed for this morning looks less likely, so I move from -3 to no change, at 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Guirassy's doubtful status and Gladbach's missing captain Kleindienst point a little lower, but less rotation risk for Dortmund softens it, so I go 2% lower, to about 9.4 (was -3).

401884734.overall: Frankfurt (10th) and Hoffenheim (9th) are level on 12 points, a mid-table game with little extra at stake; Frankfurt drew 2-2 at Paderborn before the break, Hoffenheim beat Schalke 2-1. Adi Huetter must rebuild his defence without the banned Elias Baum (counted), captain Koch is back in full training, but Can Uzun returned from international duty with a cold and hessenschau expects him to miss out, while Comunio also lists Knauff as unwell; the numbers know none of this. Hoffenheim's defence is thin: Hajdari, Hranac, Gendrey and De Cat are out, confirmed by Comunio and Bulinews, and the numbers only count Conte's absence up front, not these defenders; Prass is doubtful with a muscle problem. Max Burda referees; his short record is just below average.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. Hoffenheim are without four defenders (Hajdari, Hranac, Gendrey, De Cat) and the numbers give Frankfurt no lift for any of them, but Frankfurt now look set to lose their creator Uzun to a cold, with Knauff also unwell. I go 2% higher, to about 3.7 (was +3; Uzun's likely absence is the change).

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, already nudged up for Hoffenheim's recent count (37 in six). A reshuffled Hoffenheim defence may concede more chances but not clearly more corners, and Frankfurt's possible switch to a back three with Doan as wing-back does not point either way, so I stay at 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards, with recent counts, head-to-head and referee Burda's slightly low record already in them. Huetter wants more aggressive pressing and Hoffenheim press hard too, and both defences are makeshift, but that is only a hunch, so I stay at 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots and already add Hoffenheim's recent volume (101 in six, +12%). Hoffenheim's sporting director points to their many runs in behind and strong pressing, which is what the numbers see; the gaps in their defence affect chance quality more than the total, so I stay at 28.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Hoffenheim's missing defenders should give Frankfurt some cleaner looks, but losing Uzun takes away Frankfurt's best shooter from range, so the two cancel out and I drop this morning's +2 to stay at 10.1.

401884728.overall: Promoted Elversberg (7th, 13 points, three defeats in four) host Freiburg (3rd, 19 points, four straight wins) in the first league meeting between the clubs; Vincent Wagner calls Freiburg a 'variable' opponent and wants to stick to his own game. Elversberg have conceded 18 goals in nine games and their centre-back pairing is in doubt: Comunio has Seifert out and captain Pinckert doubtful with an ankle problem (Sports Mole has both doubtful), so Rohr and Le Joncour are expected to start; Mickelson is out (counted). The numbers also count right-back Gyamerah as out, adding about 6% to Freiburg's goals, but Comunio says he is back and the Bundesliga's predicted lineup has him starting. Freiburg miss Muslija (counted) and the banned Berkay Yilmaz, not a regular, and Julian Schuster is expected to name his usual XI. Richard Hempel referees, with only two games on record.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals and add about 6% to Freiburg's goals for Gyamerah, who now looks fit, so that boost is too big. But Elversberg may also be without both first-choice centre-backs, Seifert and Pinckert, which the numbers don't see, so the two roughly cancel and I stay at 3.2 (was -2).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, with Freiburg's recent run of corners (30 in six) already added. Freiburg's wide play through Beste and Treu wins most of their corners, which is what the numbers see, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. Referee Hempel has only two games on record, which the numbers already blend towards the average, and neither side's recent card counts stand out; a stand-in centre-back pairing for Elversberg is only a small hunch for more fouls, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, with Freiburg expected to shoot more. Elversberg have allowed 103 shots in their last six and Freiburg have been shooting above their usual level; both are already counted, so I keep 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. Elversberg score more than their chances suggest (17 goals from 14.3 expected) and Freiburg's accuracy has dipped lately (already counted); the centre-back doubts and Gyamerah's return pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.4.

401884729.overall: Schalke (17th, 6 points, one win in nine and no home win yet) host Stuttgart (8th, 12 points, back-to-back league wins after 1-0 against Bremen). Schalke have scored only five league goals and none in their last four home games; Miron Muslic gets striker Moussa Sylla, Gantenbein and Bachmann back (none expected to start), but top scorer Robin Gosens is still a question mark after his knee injury and at most a short cameo, while Becker, Schallenberg and Woeber are out (Woeber and Becker already counted). Stuttgart are still without midfield organiser Angelo Stiller and Luca Jaquez; Josha Vagnoman has trained with the group again for several days and Leo Sauer trained fully on Thursday, but the expected XI has neither. Sebastian Hoeness expects a passionate, physical Schalke backed by 60,000 fans; Daniel Siebert referees, and his slightly higher card record is already added.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off for Woeber at Schalke and Stiller and Vagnoman at Stuttgart, and add a little for Becker missing in Schalke's defence. What they can't see is that Gosens, Schalke's top scorer, is doubtful and at best a cameo for a side that has not scored at home in four games; Sylla's return from the bench and Vagnoman being back in training only partly offset that, so I trim 3%, to about 2.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Stuttgart expected to win about 6 of them. Schalke defend deep and counter, which hands the visitors corners, and Stuttgart's wide players Fuehrich and Leweling push play to the flanks, but both habits are already in the teams' records, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards and already add about 8% for referee Daniel Siebert (4.1 a game) plus a little for Schalke's recent games. Hoeness expects an intense, physical Schalke in front of a full house, but that is how they play every home game and it is in their record, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. Schalke's attack produces few shots and may be without Gosens, and Stuttgart still miss their main midfield passer Stiller; the numbers count Stiller only for goals, not shot volume, so I trim 2%, to about 27.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target and already cut Schalke's for their poor recent accuracy (13 on target in six games). Gosens doubtful and Stiller out make both build-ups a bit poorer, and Sylla is only a bench option after missing five games, so I trim 3%, to about 9.3.

401884733.overall: Two struggling sides: Augsburg (14th) are seven games without a win under Manuel Baum and have dropped 15 points from winning positions, the most in the league, after a 5-2 loss at Leipzig; Mainz (12th) have lost four in a row, including a DFB-Pokal exit at Bochum. Augsburg have scored in every game but conceded 20 in their last eight; Matsima and Banks are out and Gouweleeuw and Massengo doubtful, while top scorer Gregoritsch is expected back in the lineup. Mainz are without holding midfielder Dominik Kohr and have Posch and Mwene back from bans. Martin Petersen referees, and his high card record (4.5 a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already high: they add momentum for both leaky defences and Matsima's absence for Mainz (+6%). Gregoritsch returning to Augsburg's lineup and Posch's return for Mainz roughly cancel out, so I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Augsburg expected to win slightly more at home. Nothing in the news changes either side's wide play, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, already including about 14% for referee Petersen and Mainz's recent count. I trim 3%, to about 5.0, because Mainz's combative holding midfielder Kohr is out until January and the numbers' three-year record still carries his seasons; Mainz are booked often even without him, so the cut stays small.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, already lifted by Augsburg's big recent volume (+19%) and Mainz's (+7%). Both teams play open games, which that figure already reflects, so I stay at 31.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with momentum adding for both (+13% Augsburg, +6% Mainz). Two weak defences point the way the numbers already go, so I keep 10.8.

401884730.overall: The 111th Nordderby: Daniel Thioune's Werder (6th, 15 points) host Merlin Polzin's Hamburg (11th, 12 points), the first time since 2012 both come in this high. Werder have won eight of the last nine home league meetings and three of their last four home games; Hamburg beat Gladbach 3-1 but have won one of five away. Werder are without Weiser (ruled out by Thioune, counted), Stage, Agu, Musah, Topp and others, with Grüll expected to be fit after a calf scare; Hamburg miss Remberg, Vieira and Nadir, and Poulsen, counted as out, is listed only as doubtful with a hip problem, while Vuskovic is unlikely to feature. Florian Badstübner referees: his low card record (-23%) and the derby boost (+39%) are both in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and take about 12% off Hamburg for Poulsen and 3% for Sambi Lokonga as fully out. Flashscore lists Poulsen only as doubtful and does not list Sambi Lokonga, so at least one may play; I nudge up 2%, to about 2.75.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with Werder expected to win most at home. Hamburg's back three with wing-backs El Ouahdi and Muheim is already in their record, and nothing in the news changes it, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards: they add 39% for the derby but take 23% off for referee Badstübner, who shows only 3.1 cards a game. Both sides have been booked less than usual lately (counted), so I don't add more and stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, lifted by Werder's strong recent volume (+20%). Hamburg tend to sit back away from home and let Werder have the ball, which that figure already reflects, so I keep 31.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with Werder's 43 on target in six already added (+15%). Grüll looks fit and Weiser's absence is counted, so nothing changes either attack and I stay at 10.8.

401883112.overall: A relegation fight in Encamp on Friday night: FC Andorra are 21st with 11 points and no win in four, Leganés 16th with 15 after beating Burgos 3-1, Luis Carrión's first league win in charge. Andorra are without goalkeeper Jesús Owono (12-match ban) and centre-back Diego Alende (red card), both already in the numbers, plus midfielder Théo Le Normand; reports differ on Gael Alonso (back per Thursday's previews, still a doubt per El Gol Digital). Leganés get Javi Montero back from a ban and Gharbi is an option to start, while one report says Rubén Peña and Pulido have knocks and Carrión called a few players 'a bit iffy'. Carrión wants a high press and useful possession, which could cut into the long spells of Andorra pressure the numbers expect. José Luis Guzmán Mansilla referees, and his low card record is already in the numbers; match-day news changed nothing in the view.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already add about 6% to Leganés' goals for Alende's ban. Andorra have conceded 24 in 13 and keep giving away early goals, while Leganés have Millán in form and Montero back; but with Gael Alonso back and Bomba expected to start, Andorra's back line is not as patched-up as feared, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 5.8 of them Andorra's, as a home side that usually has the ball and pushes up. Carrión wants Leganés to keep the ball and press high, which could trim Andorra's share a little, but Leganés' recent habit of conceding corners is already in momentum (+3.9%), so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards: both sides have been booked a lot lately (+11% and +6.6% momentum) and the referee, José Luis Guzmán Mansilla, averages 4.7 cards a game, which already takes about 13% off. It is a tense game between two bottom-five sides, but the previews point to no extra needle beyond that, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, about 18 of them Andorra's, which assumes Leganés sit deep. Carrión said on Thursday he wants a high press and more action in the opponent's half, and Manso also noted Leganés now keep more of the ball, so Andorra may get fewer long spells of pressure; I trim a little, to about 26.4. Leganés' high shots conceded lately are already in momentum (+7%).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, with Andorra's recent accuracy already in momentum (+7.4%). With Bomba and Gael Alonso available, Andorra's defence should be close to its usual shape apart from Alende, who is already counted, and the small trim to shots is too little to move this, so I stay at 9.6.

401882299.overall: Granada arrive 3rd with 26 points, six straight league wins and only one goal conceded in their last five, with Jorge Pascual scoring five in his last seven; Pacheta expects a hard game against the side he calls the hardest-running in the division. Sabadell are 14th with 18 points, five league games without a win and only 12 goals in 14 games, though still unbeaten at home. Ferran Costa has about a third of his squad injured (Quadri, Urri and others, of whom the numbers only know Gioacchini) plus Català's ban, which the numbers count; they did win 3-0 at Utebo in the Copa on Wednesday, so legs may be a little heavy. Granada get left-back Diallo and forward Arnaiz back on the bench but still miss Casadesús, and Owen Emeka is away with Spain's U17s. No referee had been named in the pages I read.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals and already take about 13% off Sabadell's goals for Gioacchini, and their momentum already counts Granada's tight defence (one goal conceded in five). Sabadell's other absences cut both ways: fewer attacking options but a thinner defence against an in-form Pascual, so I see no clear direction and stay at 1.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, 4.9 of them Sabadell's. With roughly a third of the squad injured, most of it unknown to the numbers, and a Copa tie in their legs from Wednesday, Sabadell may spend less time pinning Granada back, so I keep a small trim to about 8.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards and already add a little for Sabadell's busy recent card count while taking some off Granada's quiet one. Sabadell run and foul a lot, and tired legs could bring late fouls, but that is a hunch and no referee has been named, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots, 17 of them Sabadell's, which assumes a normal home side. Sabadell are missing many players the numbers don't know about and played on Wednesday, while Granada's defence has been very hard to break down, so I still expect less volume from the hosts and trim to about 25.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. A thin, tired Sabadell side should create a little less against a Granada team that has conceded once in five, but accuracy moves less than volume, so I trim only a little, to about 7.6.

401883108.overall: A bottom-of-the-table six-pointer at Zubieta: Real Sociedad II are 18th with 13 points and three games unbeaten, Cádiz 20th with 11 and without an away league win in 12 games after a 1-1 at Eibar. Sanse miss Jon Balda through suspension, which the numbers count, and one preview (EFE) says Jon Ansotegi may also be without Beitia, Marchal and Dani Díaz, with players possibly called up to a first team hit by injuries. Cádiz lose left-back Sergio Arribas to a fifth-yellow ban (RFEF list) that the numbers don't know about, but get Jandro Orellana, Bojan Kovacevic and Álvaro García Pascual back, and Manu Rivera, whom the numbers treat as injured, has been playing. Borja Jiménez expects an open game between two young sides; no referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and already adjust for Balda's ban. I had added a little for Arribas' ban and an open game, but one preview now says Sanse could be short of Beitia, Marchal and Dani Díaz too, which would blunt the home side as much as Arribas weakens Cádiz, so I drop that and stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 5.5 of them Sanse's as the home side with more of the ball, and already add some for Sanse's busy recent run (38 in six games). Nothing in the previews changes how either team attacks wide, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. Both teams foul a lot (Balda and Arribas are both out after five yellows), and a bottom-three fight between two nervous young sides adds a little edge their averages may not fully show; no referee is named yet, so I keep a slight lift to about 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, about 18 of them Sanse's, already lifted for their heavy recent shooting. An open game would add some shots, but Sanse's possible absences and Cádiz getting Orellana and Rivera back to keep the ball point the other way, so I stay at 27.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I had nudged it up because Arribas' ban unsettles Cádiz's left side, but a possibly weakened Sanse attack offsets that, so I go back to 8.3.

401882301.overall: Castellón are 2nd with 30 points, unbeaten at Castalia, with the league's best defence (5 conceded in 13) and a 1-0 win at Valladolid last weekend; a win would put them top for at least three nights before leaders Almería play Ceuta on Monday. Eldense are 15th with 17 points after beating Sabadell 2-0, but have lost their last two away games and now lose captain and centre-back Jesús Clemente (dislocated shoulder) and Fidel Chaves (muscle problems), neither of which the numbers list; Guirao is back. Castellón are without Brignani (in the numbers) plus Fran Castillo, Rodrigo Rêgo and Isra Suero, a 6-goal midfielder who also missed the Valladolid win and is not in the numbers' list. Referee Pablo Morales Moreno (4.6 cards a game in 7) is already counted, and Javi Calleja promises a man-to-man press and no fear. The two sides' new absences roughly cancel out, so the view stays close to the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 2.0 of them Castellón's, with Brignani's injury already counted. Two absences the numbers don't know about pull in opposite directions: Castellón miss Isra Suero (6 goals in 686 minutes, though they won at Valladolid without him), while Eldense lose captain and centre-back Jesús Clemente to a dislocated shoulder. They roughly cancel, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 5.7 of them Castellón's; they are one of the division's best possession sides at home and won 9 corners at Valladolid without Suero. Calleja says Eldense will press man-to-man rather than sit deep, which could cut a few home corners but also open the game, so nothing clearly points either way and I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, with Eldense's heavy recent card count (20 in their last 6) and referee Pablo Morales Moreno's lower average (4.6 a game in 7, -5.4%) both already counted. Eldense's risky man-to-man press against a possession side can bring fouls, but that is how they have played all season, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.5 shots, 14.9 of them Castellón's. Castellón had 15 shots at Valladolid without Suero, and Eldense's press may give both sides chances, but with absences on both sides offsetting I stay at 24.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Castellón's defence allows very little and Eldense are without Fidel Chaves in attack, while Castellón miss Suero's finishing and Eldense lose Clemente at the back; these balance out, so I stay at 8.7.

401883107.overall: Tenerife (13th, 18 points) are still grieving forward Jesús de Miguel, who died after the 2 November game with Andorra; in their first match since, Álvaro Cervera's side beat Ceuta 2-0 to end a run of five draws, and captain Enric Gallego (eight goals) carries their attack. Goalkeeper Dani Martín, banned for that game, should be back, and Ranos and Dani Fernández return from international duty, while Baba was still recovering last week. Mallorca, under Luis García, are 7th with 23 points and the stronger defence (10 conceded), but drew 3-3 with Córdoba last time out and have been described as inconsistent; Morlanes and Jan Salas are out and already in the numbers. News was thin: I found no Mallorca team-news page or match preview yet, and no referee is named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals: Tenerife have scored and conceded 17 each, Mallorca have the tighter defence, and five of Tenerife's last six league games were draws. The 3-3 with Córdoba was unusually open for Mallorca, but nothing new on either side's squad points either way, so I stay at 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, split almost evenly. Neither side's set-up looks set to change, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, with Mallorca (37 yellows) more booked than Tenerife (30). An emotional home crowd at the Heliodoro could add some heat, but that is already part of a normal home game and no referee is named, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.5 shots, a low total for two cautious sides. Tenerife's return to winning form and Dani Martín's return don't change the expected volume, so I stay at 22.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.7 shots on target. With Gallego leading Tenerife's line and Mallorca's known absences already counted, I have no reason to move this and stay at 6.7.

401882300.overall: Mid-table neighbours one point apart: Córdoba (10th, 20 points, 25 scored and 25 conceded) are unbeaten in five league games after a 3-3 at Mallorca, while Oviedo (9th, 21 points) lost 1-2 at home to Girona in Raúl González's debut after Julián Calero was sacked; Raúl wants a pressing, direct team. Cordópolis notes both teams have been hurt by opposition substitutes (seven goals conceded from the bench each) and Córdoba have been much weaker after half-time. Córdoba's top assister Cristian Carracedo was reported doubtful with a leg injury earlier this week and I found no update since; Oviedo still miss Dani Calvo and Chris Ramos, which the numbers already count. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, a high total for two open sides, and already adjust for Calvo and Ramos. Carracedo, Córdoba's main creator, was doubtful earlier in the week and the numbers don't know about it, but with no update since I keep only a small trim, to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners, 7.3 of them Córdoba's, a side that pushes full-backs high at El Arcángel. Raúl's pressing, direct Oviedo could create more transitions, but that does not clearly change corner counts, so I stay at 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.3 cards, already high for two teams that have been booked a lot. A new coach asking for pressing can mean more fouls, but one game under Raúl is too little to size, and no referee is named, so I stay at 6.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, a very open game. Córdoba's second-half dips and both benches' habit of changing games are already in the teams' records, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target. If Carracedo misses out, Córdoba lose their best supplier of chances, so I trim slightly to about 10.3, keeping it small because his status is unclear.

401882298.overall: Sporting (8th, 23 points, only 16 goals scored) host Las Palmas (11th, 20 points), whose three-game winning run under Albert Sánchez ended with a 1-0 loss at Granada in which Opoku was sent off. Sporting, under Nicolás Larcamón, have up to eight absences: Otero (second game of his ban) and Corredera (appeal rejected) are suspended, and Pablo García, Casas, Konrad, Gelabert, Manu Rodríguez and Alejo Sarco are injured, Sarco not yet back in group training (Infobae, Thursday). The numbers already count Otero, Corredera, Sarco and Manu Rodríguez, but not Gelabert, Konrad or Pablo García; Andrés Ferrari could make his first start after injury. Las Palmas miss Opoku (ban) and Sandro Ramírez among others, both on the brief's list. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already take a lot off Sporting's attack for Otero, Corredera and Sarco. On top of that Gelabert, Konrad and Pablo García are out and the numbers don't know it, which thins Sporting further, so I trim a little more, to about 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Las Palmas like to keep the ball through Manu Fuster and Sporting will still push at home, but the absences don't clearly change how either side earns corners, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. Both sides have had players sent off or banned recently (Otero, Corredera, Opoku), but those were one-off incidents and no referee has been named, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, 14.7 of them Sporting's. With three more Sporting players out than the numbers know about and their forwards Otero, Casas and possibly Sarco missing, I expect a little less volume and trim to about 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Sporting have struggled to score all season and are missing several attacking options beyond those counted, so I trim slightly to about 8.1.

401883109.overall: A top-five meeting: Girona (4th) and Eibar (5th) are level on 24 points, Eibar with a game in hand (their match with Castellón was postponed after Jesús de Miguel's death) but no win in their last five league games, the latest 1-1 at home to Cádiz. Quique Álvarez's Girona won 2-1 at Oviedo without Vanat and Holmes, who were on international duty and should be back. Girona miss Álex Moreno (fifth yellow), Bryan Gil, Jastin García and Furtado, all already in the numbers. Eibar, coached by Jokin Aranbarri, were without Elijah Gift, centre-back Unai Elgezabal and left-back Juan Bernat through injury last weekend, which the brief does not list. No referee is named yet and team news for this match was thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already adjust for Girona's absences. Eibar were missing two regular defenders, Elgezabal and Bernat, at the weekend and the numbers don't know about it; with no update this week, I only add a little, to about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 5.8 of them Girona's as the side that usually controls the ball at Montilivi. Nothing in the news changes that, so I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards, with Girona (35 yellows) more booked than Eibar (25). A top-five game has some edge, but no referee is named and nothing points to extra tension, so I stay at 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, 18 of them Girona's. Vanat and Holmes returning helps Girona, but they were part of the side the ratings know, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Eibar's defensive absences could give Girona slightly better chances, but I have already reflected that in goals and the effect on accuracy is small, so I stay at 9.1.

401883304.overall: Celta Fortuna (17th, 13 points, no win in five) host Valladolid (12th, 18 points) at Balaídos; Fredi Álvarez's reserve side sit just above the relegation places and usually play reactively. Celta Fortuna's medical report (19 November) lists only Somuah, Gavián and Khayat as injured, so they are otherwise at full strength. Fran Escribá's Valladolid miss Thiago Ojeda (fifth yellow), Latasa and Guille Bueno, all in the numbers, and also right-back Trilli, who strained an adductor against Castellón and is not in the numbers; Escribá has no natural replacement and called up academy players, while Balboa and Homam were away on international duty this week. Both squads are heavily booked (Celta Fortuna 42 yellows, Valladolid 41 and 4 reds), and no referee is named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already take Latasa's and Ojeda's goals off Valladolid. Valladolid also lose right-back Trilli, with no natural replacement, which the numbers don't know about, so I add a little for Celta Fortuna's chances, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, with Valladolid expected to win more of them as Celta Fortuna sit back. Trilli's absence may change Valladolid's right side, but not clearly their corner count, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.5 cards, already high because both teams are among the most booked in the league. A relegation-tinged game adds some edge, but that is in their records and no referee is named, so I stay at 6.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, split fairly evenly. Valladolid's internationals returning late in the week and Trilli's absence don't clearly change the volume, so I stay at 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Apart from the small lift in goals for Valladolid's patched right side, nothing changes how accurate either side should be, so I stay at 9.8.

401876395.overall: A relegation six-pointer opens the round: Troyes are 17th with 8 points and Le Havre last with 2 after six straight league defeats. Valérien Ismaël takes charge of Le Havre for the first time; his past sides pressed hard and he is still choosing between a back three and a back four. Le Havre's own preview lists Pembélé, Rassoul Ndiaye, Nakamura and Mosengo out and Ouziad doubtful, with Jelert back, while Mpasi, Mambimbi and Zagadou are long-term absentees. For Troyes, Junior Diaz is suspended (already counted) and forward Yacouba Koné is a doubt; Troyes have scored only 7 league goals, and Ligue 1's own figures show these two have the league's lowest shot conversion. Referee Jérémie Pignard (4.4 cards a game) is already in the numbers; no match-day news changed the view.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Troyes have scored just 7 in 10 league games and may lack forward Koné, and these are the two sides with the lowest shot conversion in Ligue 1, while Ismaël's first job will be to tighten a Le Havre side missing four midfielders. I go a little lower, to about 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, with Troyes at home doing most of the pushing. Neither side's style changes much for this: Troyes build slowly and Le Havre will defend deep under a coach in his first game, which the numbers already reflect, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards and already add Pignard's strict record (+17%). On top of that this is a bottom-two scrap where both sides need points badly and Ismaël's teams are known for intensity and pressing, which the numbers' stakes flags do not cover; a small lift to about 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots. Troyes create few big chances and Le Havre will be careful, but both will also have to chase points late on, so the two pull against each other and I stay at 24.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Troyes have the league's weakest attack and may be without Koné, and Le Havre's forwards get little support with Ndiaye, Nakamura and Mosengo out, so I trim slightly to about 7.5.

401876398.overall: Leaders PSG (23 points, five straight league wins and eleven in a row in all competitions) visit sixth-placed Nice (17 points), who have won five of their last six league games under Olivier Pantaloni. The news has changed since this morning: PSG's Friday medical report clears Dembélé, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, Doué and Akliouche, and Luis Enrique said only Kvaratskhelia and Longoni are missing, so the numbers (which only take Kvaratskhelia off) are now close to right on availability. Luis Enrique also said he will look at each player's minutes, and with Roma at the Parc on Wednesday, French reports expect the returning stars on the bench and a rotated XI with Mayulu, Ndjantou, Ferran Torres and Godts. Nice are without Abdelmonem (hamstring, not risked) plus long-term absentees Bombito, Abergel and Mendy, all already in the numbers; Boudaoui and Abdi may return. Referee Jérôme Brisard (4.2 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, with PSG's strong scoring run and Kvaratskhelia's absence (-4%) already counted. Dembélé, Doué and Akliouche are now fit, so I cut my trim from -3 to -2, but they are expected to start on the bench with Roma on Wednesday, so the first hour likely belongs to a younger PSG front line; about 3.0 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, driven by PSG's possession against a Nice side that has been strong at home. Rotation changes who attacks more than how often PSG push Nice back, and Nice's form and missing defenders are already in the numbers, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards and already include Jérôme Brisard's slightly above-average record (+9.5%), Nice's recent rise in cards and PSG's low count. I found nothing new on discipline or the referee, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, already raised for both sides' recent shooting. PSG will still have most of the ball, but a rotated starting XI after the international break, with stars managed before Roma, should be a little less sharp; a small cut to about 29.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target and already give PSG +20% for 60 on target in their last six. Dembélé and Doué, their most dangerous shooters, are fit again but likely to start on the bench, so I keep a small trim, now -2 instead of -3, to about 12.1.

401876399.overall: Monaco (7th, 16 points) have not won in five league games under Filipe Luís and have not kept a clean sheet in eight, although they are unbeaten in the Conference League and travel to Hearts next Thursday. Auxerre (14th, 10 points) under Will Still have lost two in a row, including 5-1 at Strasbourg, and have conceded a league-high 24 goals. Monaco are without Golovin, Idumbo and Ansu Fati (all counted), with Mawissa doubtful and Dier, Camara and Balogun fit; Auxerre miss Okoh, Dioussé, Fofana and Zaddy, and striker Danny Namaso faces a late fitness test on a swollen ankle. The numbers count Namaso fully out (about -19% on Auxerre's goals), but two of three previews still put him in the starting XI. Referee Jérémy Stinat (4.1 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and take almost a fifth off Auxerre's attack for Namaso, who is only a doubt and named in two predicted lineups. Add Monaco's eight games without a clean sheet and Auxerre's leaky defence, and I lean slightly higher, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Monaco expected to have most of the ball against a back three. Nothing in the news changes how either side plays wide, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards and already add Stinat's slightly strict record and past meetings. Auxerre's Dioubaté is back from suspension and Monaco's Coulibaly is available, but neither changes the picture, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.9 shots. Monaco without Golovin lose some creativity, which is already counted, and Auxerre usually sit in and break; nothing new points either way, so I stay at 23.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. If Namaso plays, Auxerre have more of a threat than the numbers allow for, against a Monaco defence that concedes every week, so I nudge it up to about 9.5.

401876403.overall: Lens (11th) and Toulouse (12th) are both on 13 points, but Lens arrive in turmoil after a 9-1 Champions League defeat at Como, the sacking of Yannick Cahuzac and the arrival of Didier Digard, whose first game this is after a week of training. Digard has not won any of his last nine Ligue 1 games as a coach and his teams are built to be organised and hard to beat; reports say he may hand a start to Mezian Mesloub. Lens are without Édouard, Bulatovic and Nawrocki (counted), with Ganiou and Sima doubtful and Ivanović back from concussion. Toulouse (Jens Berthel Askou) have Dønnum and Amougou back and only Messali out (counted), and referee Bastien Dechepy (4.4 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, partly because Lens have leaked heavily lately. A new coach's first priority after a 9-1 defeat is usually to close up the defence, and Digard's sides tend to be compact, while Sima is a doubt in attack, so I lean slightly lower, to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Lens' wing-back system and Toulouse's direct play both produce some corners, and nothing in the news changes that, so I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards and already add Dechepy's strict record (+15%) and past meetings. A new coach brings more energy but also more discipline, and I found nothing that points either way, so I stay at 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. Toulouse create plenty but finish poorly, and Lens under Digard are likely to be more cautious; these balance out, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. With Lens expected to sit more compactly in Digard's first game and Toulouse's attack wasteful in front of goal, I trim slightly to about 8.5.

401876402.overall: Second-placed Lille (21 points), the league's best defence with 7 goals conceded and unbeaten at home, host fifth-placed Lyon (17 points), who have lost their last three away league games. Lyon have a new coach: Carlos Vicens, a former Guardiola assistant, replaced Paulo Fonseca during the break and has said he will keep the four-man defence; this is his first game. Lyon are without Mata, Openda, Morton, Sulc and Ouédraogo, with Tagliafico doubtful after returning late from Argentina duty; Lille miss Tiago Santos and Igamane, and Ayase Ueda is only doubtful after a month out (the numbers count him out). Lille host Bayern in the Champions League next week, and François Letexier (4.0 cards a game) referees, already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off Ueda, Tiago Santos, Sulc and Openda. Lille's tight defence against a Lyon side that struggles away and starts under a new coach points to a low-scoring game, which the numbers already show, so I stay at 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Both sides play a 4-3-3 with wide forwards, and Vicens has said he will not change Lyon's system, so I see no reason to move from 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, with Letexier's near-average record already in. Lyon fans are banned from travelling, which takes some heat out of the stands, but that is a small thing either way, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 21.9 shots. Lille's possession game and Lyon's new coach wanting an ambitious style could add a few, but Lyon's injuries in midfield and attack take them away, so I stay at 21.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Ueda, if he plays, is likely to come off the bench only, and Lyon's attack lacks Openda and Sulc as the numbers already assume, so I stay at 8.3.

401876396.overall: Strasbourg (13th, 10 points, five defeats in six) sacked Hugo Oliveira on Wednesday evening and appointed Vítor Matos from Swansea, who starts with this home game after barely two days with the squad. Brest (9th, 15 points) arrive in form after wins at Lorient and 2-0 against Lyon. Strasbourg have the fourth-best attack but the 16th defence; Panichelli is out and Fabio Baldé, goalkeeper Jørgensen and Reyna are doubts, while Brest miss Chardonnet and Le Guen with Sa. Diop doubtful, mostly already in the numbers. Azzedine Souifi referees; the numbers know only four of his top-flight games and blend them with an average record.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, a high figure driven by Strasbourg's open games. A coach who has just arrived usually starts by trying to stop the bleeding at the back, so I lean slightly lower, to about 3.2; Panichelli's absence is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. I found nothing about Matos changing the shape at once (both teams are expected in a 4-3-3), so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Souifi has only four games in the numbers, which already blend his record with an average referee, and I found nothing that suggests a heated game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. A new-coach lift at home could add some energy, but a more cautious setup takes some away, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. With Strasbourg likely to be more careful under a coach in his first game and their main striker Panichelli out, I trim slightly to about 8.6.

401876397.overall: Third-placed Paris FC (20 points, unbeaten at home) host Angers (16th, 8 points), who are winless in five and have not scored in their last three games. Liam Rosenior's side lean on Lassine Sinayoko, the league's top scorer; Ikoné played a friendly and is back, Sangui returns too, while Chergui and Adama Camara are doubts. Angers (Stéphane Gilli) miss the suspended Lefort (counted) and Bané Diatta, with Ousmane Camara doubtful; striker El Ouazzani is back in the squad but may start on the bench behind Peter. Angers are expected in a five-man defence away from home. Referee Aurélien Petit (2.5 cards a game in four games) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already add a little for Lefort's absence in Angers' defence. Angers have not scored in three games and will sit in a back five, but Paris FC are strong at home with Sinayoko in form and Ikoné back; the two pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Against a deep five-man defence Paris FC are likely to have long spells of pressure out wide, which tends to produce corners, so I nudge it up to about 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and already take some off for Petit's lenient start. Nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots, with Paris FC doing most of the shooting. Angers' attack has dried up, but Paris FC should get more shots against a deep block; I stay at 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Sinayoko is in form and Ikoné is back for Paris FC, while Angers have barely tested goalkeepers lately; these balance out, so I stay at 8.8.

401876401.overall: A Breton derby between Lorient (10th, 15 points) and Rennes (8th, 16 points), one point apart. Rennes have won one of their last five without top scorer Estéban Lepaul (7 goals in 7 games), who is back in full training and expected to return here; the numbers do not count him as missing. Rennes' chairman has put Franck Haise under public pressure, and they have conceded 21 league goals; Frankowski is doubtful and already counted out. Lorient (Alexandre Dujeux) miss Isaak Touré and Katseris, with Ibrahima Baldé doubtful (the numbers count all three out). The numbers do not flag this as a derby, and Marc Bollengier (4.1 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and take Ibrahima Baldé off Lorient though he is only a doubt. With Lepaul back for Rennes and their defence leaking 21 goals in ten games, I lean slightly higher, to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Both sides play with wing-backs, which the numbers already reflect, and nothing in the news changes that, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards with Bollengier's record in, but they do not treat this as a derby. Breton derbies are usually fierce and Rennes are under pressure after a poor run, so I add a little, to about 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Lepaul's return helps Rennes' finishing more than the number of shots, and Lorient's style is unchanged, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. A sharp striker like Lepaul back in the side should turn a few more efforts on target, so I nudge it up to about 9.2.

401882805.overall: Athletic (7th, 16 pts, a game in hand) host Espanyol (13th, 12 pts) on Friday night at San Mamés; a win would lift them into 6th. The main match-day change: Aitor Paredes is back in Terzic's 23-man squad after muscle discomfort, along with Nico Serrano, while Yeray, Yuri and Berenguer rejoined full training; Vivian (soleus), Guruzeta, Sannadi and Egiluz stay out. The numbers still take Paredes off, so part of that cut comes back. Espanyol miss Kike García and Calatrava, Urko is a serious doubt and Carreras awaits clearance, while Expósito (counted as out) and Puado are close; Eder Sarabia, appointed on 28 October, sits on the bench after a ban and has taken four points from two games. Mateo Busquets Ferrer referees; the numbers already add a lot for his high card record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and take about 8% off Athletic's scoring because they count Aitor Paredes as out. He is now in the squad (named in Friday's list, per FútbolFantasy and ElDesmarque) and likely to start with Vivian injured, so most of that cut comes back; with Puado fit for Espanyol I go up 5% (was 2%), to about 2.31 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, 6.4 of them Athletic's, and already add Athletic's corners against an Espanyol side that conceded 44 in their last six games. Nico Williams is back from Spain duty and expected to start, so Athletic's wide game at San Mamés is intact, which the numbers assume. Sarabia wants Espanyol to keep the ball more, but two games are too few to say they will concede fewer corners, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.6 cards: they add about 29% for referee Busquets Ferrer (5.8 cards a game on their record) and about 9% for Espanyol's heavy recent card count (20 in six), most of it under the previous, more combative set-up. Sarabia builds a possession side that presses higher, which usually means fewer fouls from chasing the ball, and his first game was a calm 0-0 with Deportivo. The referee is already counted, so I keep only a mild trim for the change of style, to about 6.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, 17.7 of them Athletic's, and already add Athletic's busy recent shooting (94 in six games). Athletic have no fit central striker with Guruzeta and Sannadi out, but Iñaki and Nico Williams and Sancet, who may return to the XI, take most of their shots anyway, and Espanyol's attack is thin without Kike García. Nothing new moves it, so 26.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target and already take some off Espanyol for their poor recent accuracy (18 on target in six). Roberto Fernández (six goals) and a fit Puado give Espanyol a little more threat than in recent weeks, but Athletic concede few chances at home. These balance, so I stay at 8.4.

401882806.overall: Alavés (12th, 13 pts) host Deportivo (9th, 15 pts) at Mendizorroza on Saturday lunchtime. Quique Sánchez Flores' side have gone eight league games without a win and score little; they miss Mikel Rodríguez and Facundo Garcés for the season (Rodríguez is in the numbers), while Mariano Díaz and Rebbach are back from international duty. Deportivo's top scorer Aubameyang (5 of their 15 goals) has an ankle problem: tests ruled out an injury, but he trained apart on Friday and travels with a decision left to match day. Zakaria Eddahchouri (broken wrist) and Bright Ede (hamstring) do not travel; the numbers list no Deportivo absences at all. Antonio Hidalgo expects a very even game, and no referee had been named in the pages I read.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already cut Alavés a little for their poor scoring run and Mikel Rodríguez. What they don't see is that Deportivo travel without Zakaria and Ede and with Aubameyang, scorer of a third of their goals, a real doubt after training apart on Friday (FútbolFantasy and EFE both report it). That points mildly down, to about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners and already take some off Alavés for their low recent count (19 in six games) and add Deportivo's busy run (41). corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, with Groningen's recent drop in corners already counted (-6%). Groningen are expected to press high from the start and Heerenveen to counter, which fits the numbers' even split, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already including a +39% derby boost and Alex Bos' slightly above-average record. This is a real rivalry, but both sides have been light on cards recently (counted), and nothing beyond the derby itself points higher, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, with Heerenveen's sharp recent shooting (+8%) counted. Groningen's high press and the space it leaves usually make for an open game, but that is the style the numbers have measured all season, so I stay at 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, with Heerenveen's recent accuracy (+7%) and Groningen's dip (-7%) already in. The keeper change affects how many go in rather than how many are on target, so I stay at 10.0.

401875539.overall: A game near the bottom: Telstar (16th, 10 pts) host PEC Zwolle (13th, 12 pts), both within three points of the relegation places. Telstar ended a ten-game winless run and have four points from their last two, but have conceded 17 in six home games and lost seven straight meetings with Zwolle; coach Henk Brugge's position is still described as insecure. PEC are unbeaten in four and this is Alex Pastoor's first league game as coach; he says the team needs little changing, and PEC won a friendly 1-0 against Heerenveen in his first match. Injury news conflicts: one tracker now lists Telstar's Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes as available, while Sports Mole says Alders is out and Mendes unlikely; PEC miss Rahajaan, with Floranus and Krastev doubtful. Referee Joey Kooij (3.4 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already counting Mendes out for Telstar (-3.5%) and Alders out of their defence (+6% for PEC). If both return, as one tracker suggests, the effects roughly cancel; my earlier cautious lean for Pastoor's debut fades now that he says he will keep the side that went unbeaten in four. Both teams keep few clean sheets (three in 24 between them), which the numbers already show, so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Telstar's recent drop (-3%) already counted. Pastoor's set-up is unlikely to differ much from the caretakers', and nothing in Telstar's news points either way, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already including Joey Kooij's above-average record (+11%) and PEC's recent cards. It is a tense game between two sides near the drop, but that is common at this level and nothing specific points higher, so I drop my earlier small lean and stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already lifted for Telstar's busy recent shooting (+11%), led by Tyrone Owusu's run of four goals in six. Nothing in the team news changes either side's volume, so I stay at 30.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, with both sides' recent accuracy close to normal. I had shaded this down for a cautious new-coach game, but with Pastoor keeping PEC's set-up there is no reason to, so I stay at 10.6.

401875545.overall: Fourth-placed Twente (24 pts, two behind PSV) host bottom side Willem II, who have 3 points from 12 games, have conceded 40 goals and have not won in 29 Eredivisie matches; another winless game would equal the league record held by Helmond Sport (1983-84). Willem II replaced John Stegeman with Jurgen Streppel in October and have since lost 7-0 at PSV and drawn 1-1 with PEC; keeper Thomas Didillon was listed 50/50 by an injury tracker, and Hoogma and Lachkar are out (counted). The same tracker lists Jaden Slory's one-match ban as ending before this game, so my earlier trim for his absence is removed. Twente's Thorvaldsen, Bruns and Lemkin are only 25% and keeper Unnerstall 50%; the numbers take off only a little for Bruns. Serdar Gozubuyuk's high card rate (+37%) is already a big part of the cards number.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals, already lifted for Twente's 21 goals in their last six and Willem II's 21 conceded. My earlier small trim was for Slory's ban, but he appears to have served it, and Twente's doubtful attackers (Thorvaldsen, Bruns) are offset by Willem II possibly missing keeper Didillon, so I stay at 4.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners, already up for Twente's 46 corners in six games (+6%) and down for Willem II's low output. A one-sided game with Twente camped in Willem II's half is exactly what those figures describe, so I stay at 10.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, with referee Serdar Gozubuyuk's 3.9 a game (+37%) already pushing it well above average and Willem II's 12 cards in six counted too. A side chasing a game often picks up cards, but that is already priced in, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.6 shots, already lifted strongly for Twente's 145 shots in six (+25%) and cut for Willem II's low output. That covers the expected siege, and Twente's doubtful forwards being out changes who shoots rather than how often, so I stay at 35.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, already up for Twente's accuracy (+14%) and down for Willem II's (-9%). With no new absences confirmed on either side, I drop my earlier small trim and stay at 11.2.

401875547.overall: Third-placed Ajax (25 pts) host ADO Den Haag (17th, 9 pts), who sacked Robin Peter on 2 November and beat Sparta 3-1 under interim coach Levi Schwiebbe. The numbers take a big cut off Ajax for Julian Brandt (-13%) and Kasper Dolberg (-7%); Dolberg is out for the season, and Brandt is now a real doubt: he trains only in a limited way and an injury tracker rates him 25%, the same as Steven Berghuis, while Amrabat, Kehrer and Gaaei are back in full training. ADO miss Pozo and Reischl (counted), with keeper Kilian Nikiema 50/50 and defender Pascal Mulder 75%, which the numbers do not see. Ajax play in the Conference League in midweek and visit Feyenoord on 29 November, but a strong home side is expected. Referee Erwin Blank shows slightly fewer cards than average, which is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals with Brandt taken off completely (-13% for Ajax). He is now only an outside chance to play, so I give back only a little of that cut, plus a touch for ADO possibly missing first-choice keeper Nikiema; together about +2% to 3.2. My earlier +5% assumed Brandt was likely to play.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Ajax's slightly low recent corner count and ADO's normal output already counted. Ajax will have most of the ball against a side near the bottom, which the 6.7 home corners already reflect, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, already nudged up for both sides' recent cards and down for Erwin Blank's lighter touch (-5%). Nothing new on suspensions or tension points either way, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.1 shots, already up for Ajax's recent volume (+9%) and ADO's (+7%). With Brandt unlikely, Ajax lose their main creator, which the numbers already assume, so I drop my earlier small lean and stay at 34.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target. Brandt has a small chance of playing, which the numbers rule out, and Amrabat, Kehrer and Gaaei are back to give Ajax a stronger base; a small +2% to about 10.7.

401875540.overall: Sparta (12th, 12 pts) host AZ (5th, 23 pts), who have won only one of their last five league games (4-3 against Groningen) and visit Sparta Prague in the Europa League next. AZ's absences go beyond what the numbers know: besides Hornkamp, Zoet and Resink (counted), Kees Smit is out for weeks after a groin setback (NH Nieuws), Weslley Patati and Lewis Schouten are injured, and Wouter Goes and keeper Owusu-Oduro are 50/50. Sparta lost 3-1 at ADO before the break and are without keeper Michael Brouwer (ankle), Nick Verschuren and Teo Quintero, with Julian Baas (ill) likely to play; the numbers list no Sparta absences. Referee Ingmar Oostrom's slightly above-average card rate is already counted. News for this specific match was thin; the view rests mostly on the injury lists and form.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already taking about 5% off AZ for Hornkamp and counting Sparta's 16 conceded in six. AZ's extra absences (Patati, Smit, Schouten) weaken their attack, while Sparta are without keeper Brouwer and defender Verschuren, which helps AZ; the two roughly cancel, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, with AZ's low corners conceded and Sparta's normal output already counted. Nothing in the team news changes how wide either side plays, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already pushed up for Sparta's 14 cards in six (+8%) and for Ingmar Oostrom (3.3 a game). No suspensions or extra needle are reported, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, with AZ's recent 93 shots in six counted (+8%). AZ are short of attacking depth with winger Patati, Schouten and the creative Smit out on top of Hornkamp, and a European trip follows, so I trim slightly to about 28.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, already lifted a little for AZ's accuracy (+6%). With fewer options in AZ's attack than the numbers assume, I shade it to about 9.9.

401875542.overall: Go Ahead Eagles (8th, 17 pts) host Fortuna Sittard (7th, 20 pts), who have drawn five of their last six, most recently 2-2 at home to Telstar. Fortuna are badly hit: Ole Romeny, Lequincio Zeefuik, Edouard Michut, centre-back Rodrigo Guth and Daley Sinkgraven are all out until December or January, and the brief lists no Fortuna absences, so the numbers do not see them (their recent momentum partly does).
